about: A short, finished plan that shows the sparse paths: handover without risks, one out-of-scope item, one answered question, one open PR.

run/main.title: One-click opt-out link in appointment reminder texts
run/main.objective: Patients of Harbor Lantern Clinic can stop appointment reminder texts by tapping a link in the text itself, without logging in or replying STOP. An opted-out number gets no further reminders.
run/main.approach:
Add a reminder_opt_outs table keyed by phone number, and a signed, non-expiring token that names a patient's number so the link needs no login. A public GET /o/<token> shows a confirm page and POST /o/<token> records the opt-out. The nightly reminder job appends the link and skips numbers in the table.

The token is an HMAC over the number, not a row id, so links in already-sent texts keep working after the table is cleaned up.
run/main.delivery: One PR, reminder-opt-out-link, against main. Clinic staff review; the user merges.

done_check.text: A reminder text sent by the nightly job ends with an opt-out link
done_check.note: Checked the rendered body in test_reminder_body_has_optout_link and a dry run against the staging queue.

done_check.text: Following the link and confirming adds the number to reminder_opt_outs, and the next nightly run sends it nothing
done_check.note: End-to-end test in tests/e2e/test_optout_flow.py passes; a second dry run skipped the test number.

done_check.text: A tampered or malformed token returns 404 and records nothing
done_check.note: Route tests for a flipped byte, a truncated token, and non-base64 input all return 404 with no row written.

out_of_scope: A way for patients to opt back in from the link; front desk staff re-enable by hand for now

handover.summary: All three tasks are merged into reminder-opt-out-link and the PR is open. Reminder texts now end with Stop these texts: https://hlc.example/o/<token>; confirming on that page adds the number to reminder_opt_outs, and the nightly job skips those numbers. Opt-out covers appointment reminders only, per Marisol's answer to Q1.
look_first: reminders/optout/tokens.py: the HMAC scheme and how the secret is read

tasks/T1.title: Opt-out table and signed tokens
tasks/T1.goal: Store opt-outs and make links that name a number without exposing it.
tasks/T1.approach:
Migration 0042_reminder_opt_outs.sql creates reminder_opt_outs(phone_e164 text primary key, opted_out_at timestamptz not null, source text not null).

tokens.py builds the token as base64url(number) + "." + base64url(HMAC-SHA256 of the number with OPTOUT_SECRET). Verification uses a constant-time compare. The secret comes from the app config, never the repo.
tasks/T1.verify: Tokens round-trip; a flipped byte fails verification; store.add is idempotent for the same number.
tasks/T1.outcome: Done as planned. Added store.is_opted_out too, since T3 needs it and it was three lines.

tasks/T2.title: Public opt-out page: GET shows confirm, POST records it
tasks/T2.goal: A patient taps the link and confirms in one more tap.
tasks/T2.approach:
Routes GET /o/<token> and POST /o/<token> in reminders/web/optout.py. GET renders a plain page with one button, "Stop appointment reminders". POST records the opt-out with source = 'link' and renders a thanks page.

Bad tokens return 404 with no hint why. The confirm step stays because some phones prefetch links in texts, and a GET that opted people out would trigger on that.
tasks/T2.verify: Route tests cover good token, bad token, repeat POST. GET never writes.
tasks/T2.outcome: As planned. The thanks page names what was stopped (appointment reminders only), following the answer to Q1.

tasks/T3.title: Add the link to reminders and skip opted-out numbers
tasks/T3.goal: Reminders carry the link, and opted-out numbers get nothing.
tasks/T3.approach:
In reminders/jobs/nightly.py, filter the day's recipients against reminder_opt_outs in the query, not after, so skipped numbers never reach the SMS gateway client. reminders/messages.py appends the link built from tokens.make(number).

Add an end-to-end test that runs the job against a fake gateway.
tasks/T3.verify: Body ends with the link; an opted-out number is absent from the fake gateway's sends.
tasks/T3.outcome: Done. Message body went from 118 to 161 characters, which still fits two SMS segments.

prs/P1.title: Add one-click opt-out link to appointment reminders

questions/Q1.title: Should the link stop only reminders, or all texts?
questions/Q1.context: The clinic also texts lab-result-ready notices and the occasional closure notice. The spec says "opt out of reminders" but a patient tapping "Stop these texts" may expect all of them to stop. Covering everything is a bigger change because result notices go through a different sender.

options.label: Reminders only
options.cost: Small. The page must say clearly what is stopped.

options.label: All clinic texts
options.cost: Touches the results sender and needs a clinical sign-off on stopping result notices.

questions/Q1.blocks: The wording of the link text and the thanks page in T2
questions/Q1.answer: Reminders only. Result notices need to keep working; say so on the page.
